niches.name: Fish otolith (ear-stone) image & chemistry archives
niches.score_justification: Raw images + chemistry, dozens of lab collections, reader-vs-reader age gap, known-age anchors exist.

fidelity_card.RAW: High-resolution otolith photographs and LA-ICP-MS / isotope transect files on lab and institute sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One fish specimen — hundreds per collection, dozens of species, same imaging protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Age read by reader A vs reader B vs chemistry; usually only published means survive
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Known-age hatchery fish and bomb-radiocarbon validated ages

niches.headline_shape: A stone inside a fish's head has recorded every winter of its life — and two experts reading it can disagree by years.
niches.why_niche: Age labs keep their own image piles; there is no central reconciliation product, only per-lab atlases (AFORO, national collections) that never joined each other's readings.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18: Campaign 6: both flagship hosts (AFORO, Otolitos UNAM) are interface-locked databases with zero file piles; AFORO is additionally mirrored to GBIF. Fragmentation premise failed at host level. 9->7.

niches.name: Weakly electric fish EOD waveform recordings
niches.score_justification: Raw .wav is the specimen; species-specific signal; taxonomy rewritten by DNA after recordings were filed by ear.

fidelity_card.RAW: Uncompressed .wav/.mp3 electric-organ-discharge recordings with oscillogram exports, on lab and personal research sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One recorded fish — hundreds of individuals, dozens of species per expedition, one electrode protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species named by waveform at capture vs later DNA-barcode revisions of the same vouchers
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Museum voucher specimens tied to recording numbers

niches.headline_shape: A fish that 'sees' with electricity broadcasts its own name in a waveform — and the recordings were filed under names DNA later changed.
niches.why_niche: A handful of labs (Cornell mormyrids, Crampton's gymnotiforms) hold expedition piles on their own sites; no cross-lab EOD library exists.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18: Campaign 6: flagship lab (mormyrids.efishgenomics.com) deep-crawled 60 pages + Wayback audio-filter CDX — zero recordings surfaced. Premise failed at the named host. 9->7.

niches.name: Frog & toad call archives (regional fonotecas)

fidelity_card.RAW: Original .wav/.mp3 advertisement-call recordings with accession numbers, on regional fonoteca and lab sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One calling male — thousands of accessions per fonoteca, hundreds of species, standard field-recorder protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Call filed under the species name at recording vs the DNA-split taxonomy of today (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Voucher specimens and type-locality recordings

niches.headline_shape: A frog smaller than your thumbnail has a unique voice — and thousands of taped voices are filed under species that have since been split in three.
niches.why_niche: Fonoteca Zoológica (Madrid), Fonoteca Neotropical and university piles each hold their own accessions; the big platforms host photos, not these accessioned raw calls.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18: Campaign 6: CONFIRMED at score — Fonoteca Zoologica pile verified GOLD (see SHORTLIST-CAMPAIGN6-WAVE1-2026-11-18.md). Score stands.

niches.name: Salmon & fish scale image archives
niches.score_justification: A century of scale envelopes; images are raw growth records; reader ages vs known-tag fish is a clean two-rulers setup.

fidelity_card.RAW: Scale images (slides / scans) plus envelope metadata, held by fisheries labs, rivers trusts and agency image labs
fidelity_card.UNIT: One scale — thousands per river system per decade, one mounting and imaging protocol per lab
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Age read from the scale vs known age of PIT-tagged / coded-wire-tagged fish (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Tag-recovery fish of exactly known age

niches.headline_shape: A salmon carries its whole childhood — river years and ocean years — written in rings on a scale the size of a fingernail.
niches.why_niche: Every fisheries lab keeps its own scale library; the 2025 known-age validation set (254 fish) showed how rarely the big archives are ever checked against truth.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18: Campaign 6: NEFSC measurement spreadsheets are published (NOAA ODP), but the scale IMAGES — the niche's raw capture — sit on an internal NEFSC network; Burrishoole IFBA is catalogue-only on the web. Partial yield. 9->8.

niches.name: Longitudinal child growth study records
niches.score_justification: Same child measured yearly for decades — the rarest design in human biology; most collections joined one consortium, the strays did not.

fidelity_card.RAW: Serial radiographs, photographs, casts and measurement sheets per child, on growth-centre and foundation sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One child — hundreds per study, measured at fixed ages under one protocol for 20+ years
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Skeletal-maturity stage called by rater A vs rater B on the same films (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The child's known chronological age and the Greulich–Pyle / Tanner–Whitehouse atlases built from these very films

niches.headline_shape: The same child, X-rayed every birthday from 2 to 25, is a ruler for human growing that no snapshot study can replace.
niches.why_niche: Nine US craniofacial collections were consolidated by the AAOF — but the non-craniofacial series, the non-US studies and the two un-joined collections remain on centre sites, un-reconciled.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18: Campaign 6: AAOF flagship consolidated (probe), and the named non-US stray (Harpenden) is inside the formal archive (UK Data Service 9330); Nittedal has no public web host. Fragmentation premise failing niche-wide. 9->7.

niches.name: Hospital autopsy & cause-of-death ledgers (pre-1950)

niches.calibration_2026_11_18: Campaign 6: material found exactly as carded (Barts registers, 5 vols live) but published-by-design — SILVER ceiling at the flagship. Score stands; grade ceiling noted.

niches.name: River gauge recorder charts & staff-gauge ledgers
niches.score_justification: Rivers wrote their own diaries in ink for a century; chart archives sit in basin agencies, mostly unscanned or singly rescued.

fidelity_card.UNIT: One gauge station — hundreds of stations per country, weekly charts for decades, one recorder family
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Level read off the chart vs discharge computed from the period rating curve (second ruler)

niches.headline_shape: A river wrote down its own height, in ink, every hour for fifty years — most of those diaries have never been read by a computer.

niches.name: Cephalopod beak collections from predator stomachs

niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign9: Campaign 9: KILL for recovery — guides are published books, collections are physical jars; measurement piles never web files.

niches.name: Pre-DNA blood-group population surveys (1919–1970s)

fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Phase picks printed in station bulletins vs re-picks from the scans (second ruler)

niches.why_niche: Photo-finish film was working material, kept by federations and photo agencies in fragments; results books kept the verdict, not the evidence.
niches.calibration_2026_11_18_campaign10: Campaign 10: KILL — no film-strip archive on the web; strips are federation/timing custody; the niche-named PDF is a Wikipedia compilation.

niches.name: Regional bat echolocation call libraries
niches.score_justification: Raw full-spectrum calls are re-identifiable forever; regional libraries were built before the big platforms and never merged.

fidelity_card.RAW: Full-spectrum .wav call files with detector metadata, on regional bat-group and university lab sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One call sequence — thousands per regional library, dozens of species, similar detector protocols
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species ID by call analyst vs DNA / roost-emergence identification of the same bats (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Hand-released known-species reference calls

niches.headline_shape: A bat shouts its name in ultrasound every night — but half the regional call libraries call the same shout by different species.
niches.why_niche: National platforms exist, but the older regional .wav piles (bat groups, consultancies, theses) predate them and were never ingested or re-checked.

niches.name: Butterfly & moth specimen drawer imaging
niches.score_justification: Drawer photos are raw pattern data; subspecies labels from wing pattern vs DNA barcodes is a live second ruler.

fidelity_card.RAW: Whole-drawer and per-specimen wing photographs on regional museum and society collection sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One specimen — thousands per collection, standard pinning and imaging
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Subspecies assigned from wing pattern vs DNA barcode clusters (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Type specimens and barcode-vouchered reference series

niches.headline_shape: A museum drawer holds a hundred butterflies pinned in 1920 — their wing patterns still argue with their DNA about who is who.
niches.why_niche: The big barcode library covers sequences, not the drawer photography of the older regional collections where the pattern-based names were made.

niches.name: Snake venom proteomics spectra by population
niches.score_justification: Raw spectra per population; antivenom labels are a clinical second ruler; labs publish pooled profiles only.

fidelity_card.RAW: Mass-spectrometry runs and protein-family tables per venom pool, on toxinology lab sites and supplements
fidelity_card.UNIT: One venom pool — dozens of populations per species complex, similar LC-MS protocols
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species/population name on the vial vs antivenom neutralisation results (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Reference venoms held by antivenom producers

niches.headline_shape: The same snake species can be a medical emergency in one valley and far less dangerous in the next — its venom keeps the receipts.
niches.why_niche: Toxinology is a cottage industry of national labs; each publishes its own population profiles and the raw runs rarely leave the lab site.

niches.name: Heritage dendrochronology — building & art timbers
niches.score_justification: Building-timber ring series live on heritage-lab sites, outside the climate tree-ring banks; radiocarbon is the anchor.
keywords: tree ring dating historic buildings report

fidelity_card.RAW: Ring-width series files (.rwl/.txt) and dating reports for building timbers and panel paintings, on heritage dendro lab sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One timber — hundreds of dated buildings per lab, one crossdating protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Dendro date vs radiocarbon / documented construction date (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Regional master chronologies held by the labs themselves

niches.headline_shape: The beam in a 600-year-old roof knows the year its tree was felled — to the year, sometimes to the season.
niches.why_niche: Climate dendro has its bank (ITRDB); heritage dendro — houses, ships, paintings — is dozens of small labs whose series files sit beside their client reports.

niches.name: Bacteriophage plaque & host-range collections
niches.score_justification: Plaque photos + host-range tables per phage; genome labels arrived later and renamed the collection.

fidelity_card.RAW: Plaque photographs and host-range assay tables on university phage-bank and lab sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One phage — hundreds per teaching/lab collection, standard plaque-assay protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Host range by plaque assay vs host predicted from genome (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Reference host strains and typed type-phages

niches.headline_shape: A virus you cannot see leaves a clear hole in a lawn of bacteria that you can — and the hole's shape is its signature.
niches.why_niche: Phage banks are teaching-collection scale, kept by individual labs; the pre-genomic host-range tables were never re-checked against the genomes.

niches.name: Orthodontic study-cast & ceph archives (non-growth-centre)
niches.score_justification: Dental departments hold cast mountains; Angle classifications by different schools disagree on the same teeth.

fidelity_card.RAW: Study-cast scans/photos and cephalometric tracings on dental-school and society archive pages
fidelity_card.UNIT: One patient series — hundreds per department, standard impression protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Malocclusion class assigned by school A vs school B conventions (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The AAOF growth collections as the untreated-growth reference anchor

niches.headline_shape: A century of plaster teeth in department cupboards records how human jaws changed — measured three different ways by three different schools.
niches.why_niche: The famous growth centres got consolidated; ordinary teaching-department cast archives stayed local, scanned piecemeal if at all.

niches.name: Lunar occultation & graze timing reports
niches.score_justification: Stopwatch timings measured the Moon's limb for a century; IOTA's files are personal-site era and never re-reduced against modern star positions.

fidelity_card.RAW: Observer timing reports (text/PDF) on IOTA section and personal astronomy sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One event — thousands of timed disappearances per decade, one reporting protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Limb profile derived from 1970s timings vs the same timings re-reduced with modern satellite star positions (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Kaguya / LOLA lunar limb profiles

niches.headline_shape: Amateurs with stopwatches mapped the mountains on the Moon's edge to a hair's breadth — using stars that have since been re-measured from space.
niches.why_niche: Occultation astronomy is a volunteer world of section coordinators and personal pages; reductions were published, the raw timing files mostly were not pooled.

niches.name: Small-observatory glass plate logbooks & plate stacks
niches.score_justification: Plate logbooks are the index to a century of sky photos; big plate archives are famous, small observatories' are attic material.

fidelity_card.RAW: Plate logbook scans and plate-stack inventories on small observatory and university archive sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One plate — thousands per observatory, one logbook tradition
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Object named in the logbook vs what modern plate-solving finds on the plate (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: DASCH / APPLAUSE reductions for the flagship collections as method anchor

niches.headline_shape: A century of the night sky sits on glass in observatory attics — the logbooks that say what's on each plate are themselves fading paper.
niches.why_niche: Harvard and Sonneberg got digitisation programmes; the dozens of smaller plate stacks have, at best, a PDF logbook on an archive page.

niches.name: Early radio-astronomy chart recordings
niches.score_justification: Pen-chart drift scans are the raw data of radio astronomy's first decades; each observatory's charts were read once, by hand.

fidelity_card.RAW: Pen-chart / photographic drift-scan records and observing logs on observatory history and archive sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One receiver chart — years of continuous drift scans per early observatory
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Source fluxes read off charts at the time vs modern survey fluxes for the same sources (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Modern radio catalogues (NVSS etc.) as the anchor sky

niches.headline_shape: The first maps of the radio sky were drawn by pens on paper tape, in real time, by night staff — the tapes were never re-read.
niches.why_niche: Radio astronomy's history is well told but its chart archives are observatory-by-observatory, mostly unscanned, and the field moved to digital too fast to consolidate them.

niches.name: Concrete & materials test ledgers (municipal labs)
niches.score_justification: Every structure began as crushed cubes; city lab ledgers are uniform, long, and almost entirely unscanned as data.

fidelity_card.RAW: Cube/cylinder crushing-test ledgers and cement test tables in municipal and university lab archive PDFs
fidelity_card.UNIT: One test — thousands per lab per decade, standard test forms
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Strength recorded in the ledger vs the same structures' cores tested today (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Modern standards' reference curves and surviving structure cores

niches.headline_shape: Every bridge and dam was once a tray of little concrete cubes, crushed one by one — the crushing ledgers are still on shelves.
niches.why_niche: Materials testing was municipal routine, archived as paperwork; engineering history used the standards, not the ledgers behind them.

niches.name: Paint & pigment cross-section archives (conservation labs)
niches.score_justification: Layer stratigraphy per artwork; each museum lab holds its own section photos; Raman IDs are the second ruler.

fidelity_card.RAW: Paint cross-section micrographs with layer notes, on museum conservation and lab sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One sample — hundreds per museum lab, standard embedding/sectioning protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Pigment named from optical microscopy vs Raman / SEM-EDX identification (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Reference pigment libraries (e.g. published IR/Raman spectra)

niches.headline_shape: A flake of paint the size of a pinhead contains every repainting a picture ever suffered — layer by layer, like tree rings.
niches.why_niche: Conservation labs publish case studies, not populations; the cross-section photos accumulate per-lab and are never compared across collections.

niches.name: Theatre playbill & concert programme archives
niches.score_justification: Playbills are structured data in disguise (date, cast, works); small venues and libraries scanned their own runs.

fidelity_card.RAW: Playbill/programme page images on theatre, library and local archive sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One performance — thousands per venue run, one printed format for decades
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Cast as printed in the playbill vs cast as reviewed in next day's press (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Published performance annals of the flagship houses

niches.headline_shape: Every night for a hundred years, a theatre printed who sang what — the programmes remember performances no recording ever caught.
niches.why_niche: Flagship houses published their annals; the long tail of provincial theatres' programmes sits in local-library scans, unindexed as data.

niches.name: Factory payroll & wage books (local archives)
niches.score_justification: Worker-by-week wages are the raw data behind every published wage index; the books are in county record offices.

fidelity_card.RAW: Payroll/wage book scans and transcriptions on local archive, mill-museum and record-office sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One worker-week — hundreds of workers × decades per firm, standard ledger format
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Wage in the firm's book vs the published industry wage series for the same year (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Census occupational data and published wage benchmarks

niches.headline_shape: A mill's pay book knows what a twelve-year-old actually earned in 1880, week by week — the famous wage series are averages built from books like it.
niches.why_niche: Wage books survive firm by firm in local custody; historians sampled famous firms, and the rest were never transcribed as a panel.

niches.name: Polling-booth-level historical election results in gazettes
niches.score_justification: National results are consolidated at constituency level; booth-level returns sleep in official gazette PDFs.
keywords: historical election results polling station gazette
election returns by booth archive pdf

fidelity_card.RAW: Booth/polling-place return tables in official gazette and local newspaper scans
fidelity_card.UNIT: One booth — thousands per election, standard return forms
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Booth returns summed vs the officially declared constituency total (second ruler — they do not always agree)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Published constituency-level election databases

niches.headline_shape: Elections were decided booth by booth, and the booth numbers were printed once, in a gazette almost nobody kept.
niches.why_niche: Constituency databases are a mature product; the booth-level geography underneath them was never extracted from the gazette scans.

niches.name: Seed catalogue variety listings (1880–1970)
niches.score_justification: Every catalogue is a variety census with prices; variety names vs trial results is a second ruler for hype.

fidelity_card.RAW: Seed/nursery catalogue page images and listings on library digital collections (e.g. biodiversity and trade-catalogue libraries)
fidelity_card.UNIT: One variety-listing — hundreds of firms × annual catalogues for a century
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Variety praised in the catalogue vs the same variety in official trial results (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Genebank accession records for varieties that survive

niches.headline_shape: A seed catalogue from 1900 lists 300 tomato varieties; your supermarket has six. The catalogues are the census of what was lost.
niches.why_niche: Trade-catalogue libraries digitised the famous firms; variety-level extraction across the long tail of regional seedsmen was never done.

niches.name: Regional restaurant menu collections
niches.score_justification: Menus are dated price-and-dish censuses; the famous collection is one city — regional libraries hold the rest.

fidelity_card.RAW: Menu page images on regional library and historical society sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One menu — hundreds per city collection, dated by design
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Dish price on the menu vs the same dish in newspaper advertisements of the same week (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Published price indices and the flagship menu collections as benchmark

niches.headline_shape: A 1910 menu prices a full dinner below today's coffee — and lists dishes that no longer exist anywhere on Earth.
niches.why_niche: NYPL's menu project made one city's collection famous; regional libraries hold comparable runs that were scanned as ephemera, not data.

niches.name: Borehole & water-well log archives
niches.score_justification: Drillers' logs are raw subsurface truth; state surveys each host their own scans; headline is weaker, hence the score.

fidelity_card.RAW: Drillers' log sheets and borehole record scans on state geological survey and water-authority sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One borehole — tens of thousands per state survey, standard log forms
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Driller's plain-language strata vs geologist-coded lithology (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Mapped bedrock geology and modern geophysical logs

niches.headline_shape: Every farm well ever drilled left a one-page X-ray of the ground beneath it — filed county by county, never joined up.
niches.why_niche: Well logs are a known resource class, but each survey's scans use different forms and portals; cross-region lithology panels remain unbuilt.

niches.name: Individual-observer sunspot drawings archives
niches.score_justification: Distinct from the (excluded, killed) sunspot-number series: the drawings themselves, per observer, are image data with personal equations built in.

fidelity_card.RAW: Sunspot drawing sheets (observer, date, group sketch) on observatory and society archive sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One observer-day — dozens of long-running observers, daily cadence for decades
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Groups counted from the drawing vs the same observer's reported count (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Modern SDO/HMI imagery for the overlap years and the published group-number benchmark

niches.headline_shape: For 150 years, people drew the Sun's spots by hand every clear day — each drawer quietly drew a slightly different Sun.
niches.why_niche: The number series built from drawings is consolidated (and was hunted/killed as a target); the drawing sheets themselves, observer by observer, sit in separate observatory archives.

niches.name: Ship-model towing-tank test records
niches.score_justification: Towing tanks tested every hull form on paper first; university tank archives are local and film-era.
keywords: ship model basin test data historical

fidelity_card.RAW: Model resistance-test tables, photos and films on university and naval tank archive pages
fidelity_card.UNIT: One hull model — hundreds per tank, standard towing protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Resistance measured in the tank vs the full-size ship's trial results (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The surviving ships' documented service speeds

niches.headline_shape: Every great liner was first a wooden model dragged down a water tank — the drag numbers that chose its shape sit in tank archives.
niches.why_niche: Towing tanks were few and famous, but their test series were client work, archived per-institution and rarely published as data.

niches.name: Collector discographies of 78rpm & folk recordings
niches.score_justification: Enthusiast discographers documented labels the industry archives lost; their files live on personal sites, dying with them.

fidelity_card.RAW: Label discography files (matrix, take, personnel, date) on collector and society sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One side — tens of thousands per label run, one discographic format per collector community
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Session data from the discography vs the audio itself where copies survive (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Company ledgers where published (e.g. label archives) as benchmark

niches.headline_shape: The complete story of a record label may exist only on one collector's website, built over thirty years of evenings.
niches.why_niche: Discography is a volunteer literature of personal sites and society PDFs; when a site lapses, a label's session history lapses with it.

niches.name: Small-town newspaper page-image runs (non-US / pre-1923 gaps)
niches.score_justification: Page images are raw text-plus-ads; national programmes covered flagships, the local runs are library-by-library.
keywords: small town newspaper scans library collection

fidelity_card.RAW: Newspaper page-image runs on local library and archive sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One issue — thousands per town title, daily/weekly cadence for decades
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: OCR text layer (where present) vs the printed page re-read (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: National newspaper programmes' titles as the coverage benchmark

niches.headline_shape: A small town's whole memory — prices, deaths, scandals, weather — ran in a weekly paper whose scans sit on one library's website.
niches.why_niche: National digitisation took the metropolitan titles; thousands of local runs were scanned by single libraries with no shared index or OCR standard.

niches.name: Canal & inland-navigation traffic ledgers
niches.score_justification: Boat-by-boat cargo tolls are a complete trade census for the pre-rail economy; ledgers sit with canal societies.

fidelity_card.RAW: Traffic/toll ledger scans on canal society, waterway archive and record-office sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One boat passage — thousands per canal per decade, standard toll forms
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Cargo declared for toll vs cargo in the receiving port's books (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Published canal company annual tonnage summaries

niches.headline_shape: Every boat that moved coal in 1820 paid a toll and was written down — boat, owner, cargo, miles — in ledgers canal societies still hold.
niches.why_niche: Canal history is a society world; its ledgers were microfilmed or scanned locally, and the boat-level panel was never built.

niches.name: Club sport scorebooks & gate ledgers (pre-1950)
niches.score_justification: Scorebooks are the raw record behind sports databases; gate ledgers add the crowd. Club-level material is attic-grade.
keywords: football club gate receipts ledger archive

fidelity_card.RAW: Scorebook and gate-ledger scans on club, county and society archive sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One match — hundreds of matches per club archive, standard scorebook format
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Scorebook innings vs the next day's newspaper scorecard (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Published results databases (the consolidated verdict layer)

niches.headline_shape: The official history of a football club may rest on one scorebook in a supporter's attic — crowds, scorers and all.
niches.why_niche: National sports databases consolidated top-flight results; the scorebooks and gate books of the ordinary clubs were scanned, if at all, by the clubs themselves.
